_doc: Example rule: demonstrates all 7 checker types. The runner only reads checks[]; keys starting with _ are ignored and can be used as comments. This is a hypothetical target agent 'demo-agent'; it does not correspond to a real subject.

checks._comment: Exists: a class of actions appears at least once (unordered). match uses regex against the serialized action string.
Count: occurrence count falls in an interval. Here we require reading at least 3 files. min_count/max_count are both optional.
Forbidden: must not appear; a hit is a FAIL. exclude avoids false positives: here rm -rf is forbidden but occurrences mentioned inside echo/comments are excluded. Don't anchor exclude with ^.
Before: action a must occur before b (focused on one pair). a and b are each a matcher.
Milestone: hit a sequence of actions in order across the trajectory (any actions in between are allowed), gives progress score. Describes the workflow skeleton.
checks.reason_tmpl: skeleton: read config → build → test, in order

checks._comment: IfThen: conditional implication. If a appears then b must appear (order does not matter; if a does not appear, this passes vacuously). Catches 'claim matches action': claiming DONE means tests must have really run.
checks.reason_tmpl: claiming tests passed means tests must have really run

checks._comment: Produces: production layer. Only supply an artifact name; automatically matches production actions (create_file/modify_file etc.) + path containing that name. Note: files written in bulk by scripts are invisible to the hook.
checks.name: report.md
